findings.where: Whole lesson, against brief section 2 row 2
findings.what: Conduit shrink is missing from every screen and from the explain. The brief promised it for this lesson: the hypotenuse minus the run, 0.268 per unit of offset at 30° (2 − √3), set against the field tables of 1/4 and 3/16 and taught as a field allowance. The cut is recorded only in i2.critique.json, which says the research holds no shrink figures, yet research-notes.md section 7.1 has the tables. Either add one screen or amend the brief so Dan is told it was left out.

findings.where: Step 9 (The arrow and its shadows), step text
findings.what: The screen calls the shadows the force's components but never says that the two parts together act exactly as the one force does, which is why a force can be swapped for its parts. It also never uses the syllabus word 'resolve'. That sentence appears only in the dossier's explain ('textbooks add') and in the analogy's breaks, with no footnote either time.

It states the half square's 45° and the equilateral triangle's 60° top angle without the one-line reason. The two equal angles share 90°, and the three equal angles share 180°. The explain gives the second reason, but the screen skips both.

'Tilting the floor by α tilts the line square to it by α as well, so the weight is α away from that line' skips the starting fact: on flat ground the line square to the floor points straight down, along the weight. The demo, which tilts from α = 0°, shows this, but the words do not; add that half-sentence.

The SHOW paragraphs run to 90-110 words. Together with the four-line lead, they push the picture's top to about 640 CSS px (i2.a2-360-light.png shows it at the foot of a phone screen), so most of the 4.4 s demo plays out of view while Dan reads. Either trim the text or start the demo when the picture scrolls into view.

The caption 'The floor shadow is the arrow's length times cos θ ...' and the lead about the triangle, calculator and arrow stay on every screen. On the calculator, exact-triangle, cosec and slope (W, α) screens they do not describe the picture, and the lead costs four lines above each step on a phone.

sin⁻¹ is re-taught from the Bitesize quote and contrasted only with 2⁻¹ from Powers and roots. Dan already knows f⁻¹ from Functions and their graphs as 'the machine run backwards'. A one-line reminder of that would start from what he has, which is how the brief's 'Not taught again' list asks for it.

Every angle puzzle is answered by sin⁻¹ or tan⁻¹, and none by cos⁻¹, so the brief's 'mixed so you have to choose' is only partly met. Make one angle puzzle a cos⁻¹ answer, for example a rope given its floor part and F.

'Rises 1 m over a 2.5 m run' is ambiguous for an electrician, to whom a tray run usually means its length along the tray, which makes sin⁻¹ 0.4 = 23.6° a fair reading. The picture labels 2.5 m on the level, but the task should say '2.5 m measured level' too.

The brief's 'a launch split into its two parts', which Quadratics and polynomials left for this course, is on no screen. It appears only in the dossier's explain, as an unsourced 'Textbooks split a launch speed ...'. One line on step 9 or 10 would close Quadratics' loop.

findings.where: Explain and step 7, secant and cotangent
findings.what: 'Textbooks add the secant ... and the cotangent' has no footnote. The brief cites MCA 5.1.4 ('Sine, Cosine, Tangent, Secant, Cosecant, Cotangent') and Khan for the six ratios (notes 2.1, 3.3), so cite them.

The α label sits mid-wedge, about 60 px from the slope's foot, where only a small tick marks the angle. The 'W sin α ?' label also sits above the block, apart from its short bar along the slope. Both read correctly, but the label and bar pairing could be tighter.
